records.name: Autophagy
records.tldr: Autophagy delivers cellular material for breakdown and reuse. The amount present, the rate of recycling and whether cells need it to survive are different questions.
records.summary: Macroautophagy encloses cargo in autophagosomes for lysosomal delivery and breakdown. LC3 abundance alone cannot distinguish increased formation from reduced removal. Tandem fluorescent LC3 reporters exploit different responses to acidic and degradative conditions to examine maturation in cell experiments; interpretation requires appropriate controls. Flux and survival dependence need separate tests. In a randomised phase 2 trial of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. A drug trial does not by itself establish selective autophagy dependence in a tumour.

Macroautophagy encloses cargo in a double-membrane autophagosome, delivers it through lysosomal fusion and degrades it for reuse. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. Active recycling often supports stress adaptation, whereas autophagy-dependent death requires causal evidence implicating the machinery.

A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.

Product return has evidence in defined systems. In leucine-starved cultured human HEK-293T cells, Wyant and colleagues found that SLC38A9 was needed for leucine made by lysosomal protein breakdown to reach the cytosol; the response also depended on the autophagy protein ATG7. Abu-Remaileh and colleagues measured regulated lysosomal amino-acid exchange in mammalian cells. Yeast experiments identified Atg22, Avt3 and Avt4 as partially redundant vacuolar amino-acid exporters. These results support amino-acid recycling in those systems, without establishing transport of every breakdown product, secretion from the cell or guaranteed growth.

More lipidated LC3-II can reflect greater formation or slower removal. A controlled short lysosomal block and complementary tandem fluorescent LC3 reporter can help examine turnover and delivery to acidic compartments. Equal starting amounts can have different later fates. Little additional accumulation can reflect a late block, low formation or an unsuitable window; it does not establish dependence.

Flux, selected-cargo clearance and survival dependence are different claims. NBR1 experiments identify selective ubiquitinated-cargo handling, not a universal LC3 cargo census. Use time courses, viable-cell normalisation, verified lysosomal inhibition and independent perturbations; autophagy proteins can have other functions. Lower mTOR signalling can change initiation without guaranteeing completed degradation. Typical research outputs include normalised LC3-II band intensity, reporter compartments per cell and selected-cargo disappearance over time. Tested cultures are consumed or perturbed, and prolonged lysosomal inhibition can itself disturb the system. No universal LC3 or flux cutoff selects treatment.

In Karasic and colleagues' randomised phase 2 study of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel increased response rate but did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. Response was 38.2% versus 21.1%; 12-month survival was 41% versus 49%. These group results do not show selective autophagy dependence or recommend this combination.

Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. Measure completion over time with appropriate controls. Even verified flow does not establish survival dependence; after a specific perturbation, more death can support a protective role, less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that death response, and changed flow with similar survival leaves timing or compensation as possible limits.

Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. These different drugs, models and perturbations do not define one protective or death-promoting label for all tumours. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. The authors stated that replicate-based quantification and interpretation were unchanged; that statement is theirs, not an independent validation of the replacement images.

Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and the RB1CC1-encoded protein FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Klionsky's guidelines also caution that these proteins have other functions. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.

Yamamoto and colleagues found that the cargo receptor NBR1 helped direct MHC-I proteins to lysosomes through an autophagy-dependent route in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma models. This lowered the amount of MHC-I at the cell surface, where it displays antigens to CD8 T cells. In mouse experiments, reducing MHC-I or depleting CD8 T cells reversed tumour control after genetic autophagy inhibition. Chloroquine increased surface MHC-I but, alone, did not significantly reduce tumour weight in the reported experiment; its effects on lysosomes are broad. These model results do not establish that every KRAS-driven cancer depends on autophagy or that blocking it benefits patients.
records.analogy: A recycling station can hold a large pile because more material arrives or because processing has slowed. The pile is an amount; material processed over time is a rate. Neither alone tells you whether the city depends on that station.
interventions: Clinical drug studies and mechanistic dependence tests answer different questions.
Assess flux, selected cargo and survival separately with complementary controls.

records.name: Ubiquitin-proteasome system & protein homeostasis
records.tldr: Ubiquitin can change a protein's interactions, location or fate. Some tags support proteasomal destruction; tagging alone does not establish completed degradation.
records.summary: E1 enzymes activate ubiquitin, E2 enzymes carry it and E3 ligases help select substrates and assemble modifications. Chain architecture and cellular context influence the result; ubiquitination is not universally a destruction signal. Deubiquitinases can remove or remodel tags, and proteasomal degradation is a later process that needs its own evidence. A protein can fall because synthesis changes, cells are lost or degradation increases, so abundance alone does not identify the route. In targeted-degradation experiments, target binding, E3 recruitment, protein loss, proteasome dependence and sustained cellular effects are distinct observations. Proteasome inhibitors and recruited-degradation strategies intervene at different steps; mechanistic measurements do not by themselves establish clinical benefit.

notes: Ubiquitin is a small protein attached through enzyme steps: E1 uses ATP for activation, E2 carries activated ubiquitin, and E3 promotes substrate selection and transfer. Reticulocyte experiments separated these functions. E3 families differ in transfer mechanism; no single cartoon specifies all of them.

Suitable tagged cargo can be unfolded by ATP-dependent proteasomal machinery and broken into fragments, while ubiquitin is removed and reused. Other ubiquitin signals organise interactions rather than destruction, and yeast experiments show overlapping chain functions. Lysosomal autophagy and proteasomal breakdown are distinct routes.

Protein abundance reflects synthesis and removal. Measure named-substrate decay over time with synthesis, handling and viability controls; restoration of an E3 adaptor can strengthen attribution without proving direct binding or global proteasome failure. Catalytic activity per time, ubiquitinated-cargo intensity and protein lifetime in hours are different readouts. KEAP1 is one CUL3 adaptor for NRF2, so a CUL3 change cannot uniquely identify that substrate. Pulse labelling or a controlled temporary synthesis block can help estimate turnover but may cause stress. Independent perturbation and restoration help distinguish a selected-substrate effect from a secondary response; enzyme engagement alone does not establish selective killing.

In a randomised trial of 669 people with relapsed myeloma after one to three prior therapies, bortezomib prolonged median time to progression compared with high-dose dexamethasone: 6.22 versus 3.49 months. This historical clinical result does not make an arbitrary E3 variant or abundant protein a predictive treatment biomarker.

Proteasomal degradation commonly handles individual suitable proteins, whereas lysosomal macroautophagy can deliver aggregates, organelles and portions of cytoplasm. This is a distinction of machinery and typical cargo, not an absolute partition: ubiquitinated material can also be recognised by autophagy adaptors such as p62. A tagged protein, an autophagic membrane marker and disappearance of a named cargo are different observations. Bortezomib's relapsed-myeloma trial result does not predict a hydroxychloroquine result in pancreatic cancer, and blocking both routes does not by itself demonstrate selective harm to malignant cells.
records.analogy: A recycling plant with barcode stickers (ubiquitin) and a shredder (proteasome). Myeloma is a paper mill that produces so much waste it dies when the shredder stops (bortezomib). PROTACs and glues are forged stickers that get the plant to shred the cancer's own machinery.

records.name: Pathway activation state (phosphosignalling)
records.tldr: Pathway activity is a question about a specified biological response. Protein amount, individual phosphorylation sites and downstream RNA patterns provide different evidence.
records.summary: Phosphoproteomics and other protein assays can examine specified signaling modifications, with site-specific and context-specific meaning. A site can activate, inhibit, recruit a partner or have an unresolved role. Relative phosphosite intensity also depends on parent-protein amount and sample handling; it is not automatically absolute occupancy. Transcript signatures provide another, often indirect, view. Define the proposed pathway output, timing and cell population instead of equating one marker with the whole circuit.

records.name: Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and the full transcriptome
records.tldr: Bulk RNA sequencing measures captured messages pooled across a tissue sample, including contributions from multiple cell types.
records.summary: RNA carries cellular messages; bulk sequencing samples those messages from combined tissue after protocol-specific capture and preparation. Analysis assigns usable observations to genes or transcripts and applies a defined comparison scale. A change can reflect cell composition, expression within cells or both. Gene totals can conceal transcript differences, and pooled RNA does not directly establish protein localisation, pathway flux or drug dependence.

Fictional mixture exercise: in two 100-cell samples, increasing identical marker-producing lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles their stipulated marker molecules if each contributes one and other cells contribute none. This does not show cancer-cell activation. Equal RNA contribution and matched recovery are assumptions, not measured tissue properties.
Bulk RNA-seq extracts RNA, prepares a library (often cDNA), may select mRNA or deplete rRNA or capture regions; bulk does not mean equal capture of all molecules.
Reads or fragments are assigned to genes or transcripts; shared sequences make assignment ambiguous; a count table is already shaped by preparation and analysis.
A bulk signal can rise because more cells of a type contribute, expression within them rises, or both; deconvolution estimates contributions under a model and does not separate cells.
Gene-level counts can hide isoform differences; a mutant or splice product needs sequence or junction evidence.

Bulk RNA can nominate expressed targets and summarise programmes but does not establish cell origin, surface protein, pathway flux or drug dependence; zero reads is not absence; thousands of genes from one biopsy are not thousands of patients.

Fictional teaching exercise: With equal RNA per cell, a lymphocyte-only marker and 100-cell pieces, raising lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles the pooled marker (20 to 40 stipulated molecules) without changing any cancer cell.
Record sampled region and RNA integrity; research profiling differs from a validated clinical RNA test.

Record protocol-compatible preservation, sampled region, RNA integrity and material consumed by extraction. Track capture, sequence assignment, read/fragment units, normalisation and transcript calls. Preparation time varies; reference material, process controls and biological replicates test different uncertainties. Degradation, contamination, ambiguous annotation, batch and mixture shifts constrain purpose-specific cutoffs and clinical intended-use validation.

A larger raw count can be a smaller share of a library. In an invented example, ten captured counts out of 10,000 give 1,000 counts per million, while twenty out of 100,000 give 200. Keep the counted unit and library-size definition. Counts per million scale by that denominator; transcripts per million also use transcript-length information under the chosen quantification method. These relative scales are not interchangeable, do not recover the total RNA made per cell and are not protein counts. A base-two log fold change of plus one corresponds to a ratio of two, and plus two to four under the stated normalization. A reference near zero can make a ratio large while the underlying signal remains small; these are mathematical examples, not biological cutoffs.

records.name: RNA sequencing & expression profiling
records.tldr: RNA sequencing measures captured RNA messages and, with a suitable library and analysis, can examine transcript joins.
records.summary: RNA normally carries and helps process cellular messages. Sequencing captures part of that RNA information through a defined preparation and analysis. Pooled abundance, transcript structure and cell origin are separate questions. A supported RNA join does not automatically establish a DNA rearrangement, functional protein or treatment benefit.

PSI is an inclusion estimate for a defined event and denominator; local junction evidence does not reconstruct a full transcript; unfinished nuclear RNA with introns is not automatically pathological intron retention.

Failure to detect a join is informative only within coverage and sensitivity; RNA support leaves DNA mechanism, protein effect and drug benefit as separate tests.
Fictional teaching exercise: A candidate A-B junction supported by three identical amplified reads cannot be called confirmed DNA rearrangement or effective target.

Use protocol-compatible RNA and record aliquot consumption, integrity, reference/transcript versions, partners, junction coordinates and independent read/molecule support. State the event denominator for splice fractions. Low expression, uncovered joins, degradation, similar sequence and preparation/assembly artefacts constrain detection. Validate support thresholds, event classes and confirmation for the exact panel and specimen; a caller name supplies no clinical validation.

Pancreatic cancer: RNA sequencing does two jobs here, calling the classical versus basal-like subtype that predicts chemotherapy response (O'Kane 2020, Rashid 2020) and catching the NRG1, ALK, NTRK, FGFR2 and RET fusions that DNA panels miss in KRAS wild-type tumours (Philip 2022).

Lung cancer: RNA is the only reliable route to the fusions with heterogeneous partners. NRG1 fusions were found in 41 of 21,858 tumours by anchored multiplex RNA sequencing with a different partner almost every time (Jonna 2019), and the founding CD74-NRG1 discovery came from transcriptome sequencing of driver-negative tumours (Fernandez-Cuesta 2014). In small-cell disease RNA is also how the four transcriptional subtypes are called (Gay 2021).

RNA adds fusions that DNA testing misses: in 67,278 patients with both, RNA plus DNA sequencing found 21 per cent more driver gene fusions than DNA alone (Gai 2025, Tempus authors). On the large approved DNA and RNA panels the FDA approval often covers only part of what is reported: the approval statement for Caris MI Cancer Seek names DNA content only, while the maker lists RNA expression and fusions as additional features.
records.principle: A common workflow reverse-transcribes RNA to complementary DNA for sequencing. Other chemistries, including probe-based counting, require their own interpretation of the captured signal.
strengths: Captured transcript abundance with defined comparison rules
Fusion and splice evidence when the library and analysis cover the join
limitations: Preparation and RNA integrity affect recovery
RNA evidence does not directly measure protein function

records.tldr: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing profile captured messages assigned to recovered cells or nuclei.
records.summary: RNA is distributed across cellular compartments. Whole-cell and nucleus preparations sample different material and can recover different populations. Barcodes label captured profiles rather than certifying one intact cell; quality, ambient RNA and doublet checks remain necessary. Sparse capture and selective recovery prevent a complete census, and many profiles from one biopsy do not create independent patient replicates.

A barcode labels a reaction compartment and a UMI separates captured molecules from amplified copies, giving a gene-by-barcode table; a barcode does not guarantee one intact cell.

Single-nucleus sequencing samples nuclear RNA including unfinished transcripts with introns, whole cells also capture cytoplasmic messages; a mouse cortex study showed different recovery; not proof nuclei are better for tumours.
Dissociation can lose fragile cells; nuclei can come from frozen tissue; fixed-material probe methods count ligated probes and cannot reveal every variant or splice product.
A zero can be a missed molecule (dropout) rather than absence; ambient RNA contaminates profiles; a doublet combines cells or nuclei; correction does not certify every barcode.
A cluster groups similar profiles and does not prove malignancy, lineage or a clone; cancer-cell identification needs supporting evidence.
Thousands of cells from one biopsy are nested in one biological sample; splitting into two libraries does not create two patients; replicate-level aggregation is one approach.

Record compatible viable/frozen/fixed preparation, material used, chemistry, cell/nucleus recovery and quality/identity checks. Report a gene-by-barcode table with its UMI/read/probe counting unit. Cell calling, low-quality and doublet criteria are chemistry/version-specific. Selective recovery, sparse capture, ambient RNA, degradation and batch require validation; a platform name provides neither a complete census nor clinical validity.

A detection fraction uses the analysed profiles and a stated detection rule: it is not automatically the fraction of all cells in the original tissue. A profile with one immune-gene count but otherwise epithelial features is not thereby identified as an immune cell. Sparse recovery, ambient RNA and more than one contributing cell can complicate its interpretation. Check coherent marker evidence and the method of assignment; a mixture of markers does not by itself establish a new cell type. Pooling the counts from a selected set of profiles is pseudobulk. Five hundred nuclei from one biopsy can summarize that selected population, while the biopsy remains one biological specimen rather than five hundred independent patients.

Background correction estimates which part of a profile comes from free RNA in the preparation. SoupX's authors discuss deliberately overcorrecting contamination at the cost of removing a small amount of genuine signal. The estimated contamination and settings therefore need review; a corrected weak count or zero is not an infallible label of the molecule's origin.

Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

Methylation requires an appropriate preparation and analysis rather than a sequencing category name.

Ng et al. (2009) introductory scale estimates: Human genome is about 3,000 Mb; protein-coding sequence is about 1%, roughly 30 Mb across about 180,000 exons.

At a fixed budget broader territory commonly spreads reads thinner, but actual depth depends on design and usable yield; broader territory guarantees neither uniform sensitivity nor all-variant detection.
Territory labels do not specify performance for small variants, copy number or rearrangements, and conventional WGS does not automatically measure methylation.
Reduced-coverage regions exist even in clinical exome and genome workflows, including clinically relevant genes.
Fictional teaching exercise: A research genome negative at a repeat does not supersede a validated panel; a panel that never examines a fusion breakpoint cannot exclude it by a negative report.

Compare assays by accepted specimen, input consumption, designed coordinates, analysed alteration classes, local usable depth and breadth, quality filters and validated detection limits. Degradation, capture gaps and ambiguous repeats can defeat broad designs. Extraction uses material; the name panel, exome or genome supplies neither a tissue requirement nor clinical validation.

A positive control shows that the expected signal was recovered in that control under the run conditions. It does not prove that every sample call is correct. A negative sample result still needs adequate material, usable evidence at the actual position and sensitivity for the relevant alteration class. Research discovery and clinical validation for a particular specimen and use are different claims.

Lung cancer: NICE NG122 (1.2.12) says to see the National Genomics Test Directory for guidance on next-generation sequencing panels to guide treatment. In practice this is the single test that decides between tablets, immunotherapy and chemotherapy for most people with advanced non-squamous disease, which is why waiting a short time for the result is usually a better decision than starting quickly on the wrong route. The NHS explains that your hospital specialist requests the test, usually on a sample already taken.

records.name: Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
records.tldr: Staining a tissue slice with antibodies so a protein shows up in colour under the microscope.
records.summary: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) uses antibody binding and signal development to show a selected protein in a prepared tissue section. Interpretation retains which cells and compartments stain, the intensity and distribution, and the named marker-specific method. A percentage, intensity category or composite score can describe different aspects of the result. Fixation, retrieval, controls, sampling and observer variation affect interpretation. Automated quantification also needs validation for its marker, specimens and intended use. A research stain or generic score does not replace a validated clinical selection assay.

notes: There is no universal IHC scoring scale or positivity threshold. Retain antibody clone, retrieval and detection method, controls, eligible cells, subcellular location, intensity, distribution and intended use. A research stain does not automatically replace a clinical selection assay.

An H-score under the intensity-weighted convention is weak-cell percentage plus twice moderate-cell percentage plus three times strong-cell percentage, on a 0 to 300 scale. Fictional example: 50 unstained, 10 weak, 20 moderate and 20 strong cells out of 100 give 50% positive and H-score 110. Neither is a molecule count.

Bulk receptor abundance and staining mainly on blood vessels can both be correct: one measures a mixture and the other locates signal. Neither establishes target accessibility or treatment benefit. Staining also does not establish protein activity or cancer-cell dependence on that protein.

IHC makes selected proteins visible through antibody binding and signal development in a prepared section. Specificity, retrieval, detection, positive controls, internal controls and background matter. Nuclear and membrane signals answer different questions. Multiplex fluorescence adds markers but still needs validated antibody performance and cell-boundary assignment.

In the conventional Allred scheme, proportion categories are 0 for no positive cells, 1 for less than 1%, 2 for 1% to 10%, 3 for 11% to 33%, 4 for 34% to 66% and 5 for 67% to 100%. Intensity is 0 for absent staining or 1, 2 and 3 for weak, moderate and strong staining. The total is 0 or 2 to 8. In a fictional separate example, 30% positive cells with moderate staining give 3 + 2 = 5. These integer bins are a named convention, not a universal positivity rule.

Equal H-scores can conceal different intensity distributions. A negative clinical category does not establish zero protein molecules. HER2 and hormone-receptor assays have marker-specific reporting rules; current CAP breast reporting retains percentage and intensity even when an optional composite score is given.

A useful IHC result identifies the block, fixation and section, antibody clone, retrieval and detection system, eligible cells and scored compartment. Cutting and staining use finite tissue. Report the percentage, intensity, location and named scoring scale, together with expected-positive tissue, relevant internal controls and background assessment. Poor preservation, nonspecific binding, few eligible cells, heterogeneous staining and observer variation can limit interpretation. Validation must fit the assay and its intended use; a research measurement is not automatically a clinical selection test.

Staining recognises an antibody-defined molecular feature, or epitope, rather than automatically proving a complete functioning protein. In an invented repair-gene example, weaker staining in identified cancer cells than in normal neighbours supports a cell-specific signal difference if the controls are adequate. The antibody may recognise a fragment or more than one protein form, so this does not give the amount of intact useful repair protein. The relevant form and current repair need suitable measurements of their own. One validated method can sometimes answer several questions, but measuring one property does not establish every other one.

records.name: Proteomics & phosphoproteomics
records.tldr: Measuring the proteins in a tumour, which is what drugs actually hit, rather than the genes that encode them.
records.summary: Proteomics measures the proteins and phosphorylation sites in a tumour directly, using liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with isobaric labelling to quantify thousands of proteins and phosphosites at once. Mass-spectrometry proteomics (CPTAC) reveals pathway activity and ADC target abundance that transcript levels do not predict, since RNA and protein levels often disagree. Quantitative IHC and mass-spec assays of HER2 and TROP2 aim to improve ADC patient selection by measuring the actual antigen the drug binds rather than a proxy. Throughput and standardisation remain the barriers to routine clinical use, and it is still open whether protein-level selection will outperform established IHC scoring in trials. For a newcomer, proteomics measures what drugs actually hit, the proteins, rather than the genes that encode them.

records.name: Spatial transcriptomics
records.tldr: These methods measure RNA signals while keeping information about position in a tissue section. A measured spot, an estimated cell boundary and an imputed value are different kinds of evidence.
records.summary: Spatial transcriptomics measures RNA signals while retaining information about where they came from in a tissue section. Sequencing capture and imaging-based detection use different measurement units. A third approach, region-of-interest profiling such as digital spatial profiling, releases oligonucleotide tags only from regions an operator chooses; the method paper describes regions covering 1 to about 5,000 cells and panels of up to 44 proteins, or 1,412 genes with sequencing readout, on formalin-fixed tissue (Merritt and colleagues, 2020), so the result depends on how the regions were selected. The original sequencing-based method placed sections on arrays of positionally barcoded primers and kept two-dimensional position (Ståhl and colleagues, 2016); a capture spot is a positional barcode and can span several cells. MERFISH imaged 100 to 1,000 RNA species chosen by probe design (Chen and colleagues, 2015), a targeted gene set and not every transcript. Assigning molecules to cells depends on estimated cell boundaries: many methods approximate cell positions from nuclear stains, and distinguishing the boundaries of individual cells is challenging and can hamper downstream analysis; Baysor was developed to optimise boundaries from transcript composition and cell morphology (Petukhov and colleagues, 2022). Gene values imputed by aligning single-cell data to a spatial map, as Tangram does (shown in mouse brain; Biancalani and colleagues, 2021), are model outputs and not extra RNA molecules detected by the spatial assay.

Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Figure reading (fictional geometry, no platform scale): a capture spot is one barcode that can pool several cells. Imaging decodes six RNA coordinates, three for gene G and three for gene H (3 + 3 = 6), and these are coordinates, not cell labels. Moving the estimated cell masks changes which cell a coordinate is assigned to while the RNA stays fixed. Gene R is absent from the G and H panel, so a model-inferred R value is not an observed molecule, and RNA position is not protein or function.

In a fictional map, each of two regions contains twelve illustrative immune cells, but one places them within malignant nests and the other outside. Equal cell symbols do not guarantee equal bulk RNA: similar RNA is a separately stipulated condition of the example. The map supplies neither a stromal-area TIL score nor evidence of recognition or treatment benefit. A capture spot can pool several cells, and changing an estimated cell boundary can change molecule assignment while the observed RNA coordinates stay fixed.

Reveals immune exclusion, niches and cell neighbourhoods
Works on archived formalin-fixed tissue on newer platforms

A capture unit may contain contributions from more than one cell
Assigning molecules to cells relies on estimated cell boundaries
A section samples part of a tumour, and adjacent sections do not contain identical cells
Genes imputed from a single-cell reference are model estimates, not measurements
Region-of-interest profiling depends on which regions are chosen

records.name: Functional (ex vivo) drug testing
records.tldr: Functional drug testing measures a defined response to medicines in collected living material under laboratory conditions.
records.summary: Functional drug testing exposes a defined living preparation to medicines and measures a specified response. Preparations may use dissociated cells, expanded organoids or short-term tissue cultures. Feasibility, outcome agreement and benefit from using a result to choose care are separate questions and must be tied to the actual assay version, cancer, treatment and setting.

notes: Specimen and assay card. Record donor/site/time, living preparation, transport and processing, initial composition, culture history, assay version, concentrations, exposure duration, replicates and control range. Fixed tissue cannot supply living cells; whether previously frozen material can supply the required viable preparation must be demonstrated for that protocol. Input suitability and recovery must be demonstrated for the method. Testing and endpoint processing use finite material. Output needs units, denominator, normalisation and uncertainty; acceptance criteria must be defined for the actual method. Name whether the preparation is dissociated cells, a fresh fragment or an expanded organoid. Mixed samples include normal neighbours, and expansion can change the represented populations.

Handling evidence is method-specific. Ladan and colleagues collected breast tissue in their specified medium, cut 300 micrometre slices and assessed morphology, proliferation and apoptosis after three-day exposure. This is not a general transport or storage protocol for all screens. Growth-rate methods show why baseline counts and control division affect interpretation. Retain failures and exclusions; failed preparation is not clinical resistance. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ Medium, drug access and exposure duration can change the result. Mechanism-relevant controls test whether the claimed interaction can occur; absent required cells or unrealistic exposures can make an experiment uninformative even when a numerical response is available. A laboratory concentration is not a safe human dose.

Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

Restivo and colleagues generated organoids from matched fresh and slow-frozen colorectal tumour tissue from two patients with stage IV disease. Their specified slow-freezing protocol used a cryoprotectant to preserve living material, and the frozen-derived cultures took longer to form than the fresh-derived cultures. This is evidence of recovery under that protocol, not equivalence of all fresh, snap-frozen and viable-cryopreserved samples or a guaranteed turnaround. The handling history, recovery, malignant identity and assay quality need checking for the intended experiment. Preserved molecular material alone does not establish a recoverable living model. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-022-04025-0

Read a model study as a sequence of explicitly defined groups: people or specimens offered or submitted, preparations yielding a usable model, results compared with a clinical outcome, and results agreeing under the stated rule. Eligibility exclusions, absent tumour, laboratory failures, missing outcomes and people not receiving the treatment belong to different steps. State whether the unit is a person, specimen or treatment comparison; one person can contribute more than one. A percentage among compared cases cannot describe everyone originally offered testing, and an analysis exclusion is not automatically a failed culture. Keep the drug, cancer, treatment history, outcome, clock and assay version attached rather than ranking different studies as competing accuracy scores.

The prospective single-arm SENSOR study enrolled 61 people with metastatic colorectal cancer: 54 were eligible, 31 organoids were generated, 25 cultures were screened against eight drugs and nineteen showed a substantial laboratory response. Six people received an organoid-selected treatment, three vistusertib and three capivasertib, with no objective clinical responses. That observation concerns this panel and selected population; it neither establishes benefit from using the assay nor proves that every organoid method is ineffective. Guillen and colleagues' breast-model report describes a complete response in one person with metastatic triple-negative disease after a model-nominated treatment. That case demonstrates feasibility, without a comparison estimating how often the strategy helps.

Randomised outcome evidence must be assessed for the named assay and use rather than declared absent for all functional testing in solid tumours. Ranjan and colleagues reported a 2023 trial of ChemoID selection versus physician choice from the same chemotherapy list in 78 people with recurrent glioblastoma under the 2016 WHO definition. Enrolment stopped after a prespecified efficacy analysis; the intention-to-treat report gave median overall survival of twelve versus 7.5 months. Participants could provide viable tumour through surgery or biopsy, so the findings do not include every patient with recurrent glioblastoma. Cordgenics supported the assay resources, and two authors declared licensed intellectual-property interests. This is evidence for the studied strategy and population, without validating another assay, organoid system, postoperative breast decision or universal treatment rule.

Consider an entirely invented tumour-only organoid experiment from one donor and one characterised preparation, with three wells per condition. Drug A is tested at 0.1, 0.3 and 1 micromoles per litre for 48 hours with matched carrier and handling. The planned primary readout is calibrated viable tumour-cell count at the start and endpoint, with cell identity checked. Vehicle, a positive control with an expected response and a target perturbation or rescue ask different questions. Their actual results must be documented; the illustrative counts do not show that every control passed. Three wells are not three donors. This preparation supplies neither immune cells, full human metabolism nor a healthy-organ toxicity measurement, and these example exposures are not human doses.

In that fictional experiment, both groups start at 1,000 viable tumour cells per well. At 48 hours and the middle exposure of 0.3 micromoles per litre, the median across three wells is 2,000 for vehicle and 1,000 for treatment. Treatment is at 50 percent of the later vehicle count and 100 percent of its own starting count. That establishes no net increase, not 50 percent killing or absence of division. Reduced division or division balanced by death can give that endpoint; time-course and suitable division/death measurements distinguish explanations. Keep each well and its variation rather than treating the median as three independent patients.

Two matched parallel aliquots add different fictional readouts to the same comparison; they do not track the original cells individually. Mean buoyant mass is 20 picograms per measured cell at the start, 21 with vehicle and 16 with treatment, so the treated mean is 80 percent of its starting value. Metabolic signal is 100 arbitrary units at the start, 190 with vehicle and 70 with treatment: 70 divided by 190 is about 36.8 percent, a 63.2 percent reduction relative to vehicle. Neither is a killed-cell fraction. A changing population mean is not an individual-cell trajectory, and buoyant mass depends on cell volume and the difference between cell and fluid density. It is not dry mass, a count of living cells or a measurement of a particular death mechanism.

strengths: Tests a drug-response hypothesis directly in a defined preparation
Can compare several exposures when material permits
limitations: Preparation, viability, sampling and turnaround affect feasibility
Missing components can leave a drug mechanism untested
Outcome association alone does not establish clinical utility

records.name: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
records.tldr: Cell-free DNA is DNA outside intact cells in a collected sample. Tumour-derived DNA is one possible part of that mixture; its amount depends on the specimen and method.
records.summary:
Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is DNA outside intact cells in a specimen. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is the tumour-derived part of the plasma DNA mixture, rather than a different material competing with cfDNA. DNA from non-tumour tissues can contribute much of that mixture, as illustrated by Moss and colleagues' methylation-atlas study. Total extracted DNA is therefore not a tumour measurement. A finite evaluated aliquot can contain no qualifying tumour signal even when disease exists elsewhere.

Liquid biopsy describes a specimen approach. A test may track known tumour features, look for predefined mutation, methylation or fragment patterns, or profile detectable alterations. Its target coverage, origin checks, sample requirements and calling rule determine the claim. Genotyping, residual-disease monitoring and screening have different intended uses; a method label does not validate every use or locate the source of a plasma signal.

notes: Source classes: cfDNA is DNA outside intact cells in a sample, and ctDNA is the tumour-derived part of that pool, so the two are related materials and not rival tests. In healthy donors a methylation atlas of 25 tissues and cell types attributed plasma cfDNA to white blood cells (55%), erythrocyte progenitors (30%), vascular endothelial cells (10%) and hepatocytes (1%) (Moss 2018). A tumour adds DNA only when it contributes, and the tumour share may be small or absent in the sample drawn even when cancer exists elsewhere.

Scale: plasma DNA fragments show a pattern reminiscent of nuclease-cleaved nucleosomes with a peak at 166 base pairs (Lo 2010, in maternal plasma), and tumour-derived fragments are enriched at 90 to 150 base pairs (Mouliere 2018). One assay input in a breast-cancer comparison was 4,500 amplifiable copies, about 15 nanograms (Santonja 2023), and at about 3.3 picograms per haploid genome copy 1 nanogram is roughly 300 copies (arithmetic from genome size). In a fictional single-locus model with 4,500 amplifiable opportunities and target-allele probability 1 in 100,000, the expected target count is 0.045. The target-allele probability is not automatically a tumour-DNA fraction: copy number, variant multiplicity and clone representation matter.

Yield is not origin: in a fictional experiment equal 1 mL plasma aliquots give 2 and 4 nanograms of cfDNA and no tumour-attributed signal is reported. Total DNA doubled, but tumour fraction and any tumour-DNA fold change cannot be calculated because tumour attribution was not measured. A fragment's source needs evidence such as paired white-blood-cell and tumour sequencing (Razavi 2019), and a variant seen in plasma is not automatically tumour-derived.

Method card: measures selected features of plasma DNA by a stated sequencing or molecular method, from a finite plasma aliquot that testing consumes. Output is detected or not detected, variant fractions, molecule concentrations or model estimates, each with its own unit. It cannot give an all-body cell count, lesion location, viability or treatment benefit, and validity belongs to the exact specimen, assay version and intended use.

Collection conditions can change the mixture before testing: blood-cell breakdown adds genomic DNA and can dilute a tumour fraction. The NCI biospecimen practices document, revised February 2025, prefers plasma to serum. Its protocol recommends EDTA, accepts acid citrate dextrose, and advises avoiding heparin and citrate; the literature-summary section separately reports results with several anticoagulants when processing was immediate. For EDTA blood the protocol prefers centrifugation within 2 hours and accepts up to 4 hours at room temperature or 24 hours at 4 degrees Celsius; it recommends stabilising tubes for anticipated delays over 2 hours. These are recommendations for that specimen workflow, not a universal acceptance rule for every assay. Extraction and library preparation then retain only some available molecules, so the volume drawn is not the volume evaluated.

Reading an assay report starts with the specimen and collection date, the plasma volume actually evaluated, DNA quality and recovery, origin checks, and the rule that turns a signal into a call. Low shedding, damaged input or failed quality controls can limit interpretation; a failed assay is a separate result from no qualifying signal. Genotyping, response monitoring and residual-disease detection are different intended uses. In its November 2024 drug-development guidance, FDA asks for validation of the complete workflow, representative clinical samples, the input range and prespecified calling cut-offs; validation of one use does not establish another.

A useful result ledger keeps six questions together: when the sample was collected and where that date sits relative to treatment or surgery; the assay and version; the specimen, evaluated input and quality qualifications; the reported state, including detected, not detected, indeterminate or failed; the quantity, unit and numerical qualifications; and the applicable detection and quantitation criteria. Keep the report-release date separately. Two reports arriving together may describe different biological moments, and an invalid sample or failed reference build is not a negative plasma result.

In a fictional comparison, one assay reports not detected and another reports a low detected signal. That alone does not identify an erroneous test. Compare the actual samples and collection dates, targets, input, controls and calling criteria before interpreting the disagreement. A valid negative says that the evaluated sample did not meet that method's qualifying-signal rule. It cannot distinguish every possibility: there may be no residual tumour signal, too few relevant fragments may have reached the aliquot, or the tracked features may not represent the remaining cells. This reading exercise sets no repeat-draw schedule.

records.name: Cell lineage, identity and state
records.tldr: A cell’s ancestry, its type and its current activity answer different questions. Similar activity does not prove that two cells share a recent ancestor.
records.summary: Lineage describes descent from earlier cells. A cell type or identity describes a differentiated family, while a state describes context-dependent features such as activation, stress or cycling. A genetic clone has shared ancestry and can be tracked through specified genomic features; an RNA cluster alone does not establish that ancestry. Stem cells can renew and generate descendants; progenitor potential is restricted by the biological context. Differentiation develops specialized properties without requiring every change of state to become a new lineage.

Weinreb and colleagues combined expressed barcodes and transcriptomes over time in hematopoiesis; sister-cell analyses exposed fate biases that a single RNA snapshot missed. This does not identify an individual tumor’s origin from its expression profile.

Lim and colleagues studied normal and preneoplastic breast tissue from BRCA1 mutation carriers and found an expanded luminal-progenitor population. The expression profiles of BRCA1-associated tissue and basal breast tumours resembled normal luminal progenitors more than the other tested subsets. This supported a candidate population for transformation; it was not direct lineage tracing of an individual tumour. A luminal-progenitor-like RNA program does not by itself make a cancer hormone-receptor-positive.

Support a malignant-cell assignment with tissue context, a coherent marker panel, suitable normal references and quality checks, rather than one marker or cluster name. In five primary glioblastomas, Patel and colleagues profiled 430 cells and inferred broad chromosome alterations by averaging RNA expression along chromosomes against normal reference profiles. This was RNA-based inference, not a direct DNA copy count or a breast diagnostic rule. A flat inferred profile can miss a malignant cell lacking a detectable broad change; focal alterations and point mutations can also be missed. Matched DNA, pathology and spatial evidence can corroborate an assignment, but bulk DNA does not identify every RNA barcode. Mixed markers may reflect ambient RNA or doublets. In another fictional mixed sample, vimentin RNA could come from fibroblasts or a changed cancer-cell programme. Even cell-attributed expression of that marker alone does not establish invasion, resistance or ancestry. Keep uncertain assignments uncertain.

In a fictional set with separately established shared genetic ancestry, one cell is cycling and another is noncycling. Different activity labels do not require different ancestry. Conversely, two cells in the same RNA cluster need not belong to the same genetic clone. The origin of the ancestry label matters: expression resemblance alone does not establish it.

records.name: Epithelium, stroma and tissue compartments
records.tldr: Tissue contains different cell groups and supporting material. Knowing which compartment produced a signal helps explain what the result can mean.
records.summary: Epithelium forms linings, coverings and glands; an epithelial cell is not necessarily malignant. A basement membrane is extracellular supporting material beneath an epithelium, distinct from each cell’s lipid membrane. Stroma includes supporting cells, extracellular matrix and vascular structures, rather than only collagen or fibroblasts. Immune cells and other nonmalignant cells can contribute to a tumor specimen. The relevant compartments depend on the tissue and disease.

Spatial review and suitable cell markers help test attribution; a mixed-tissue result should not automatically be assigned to cancer cells. Normal and cancer breast atlases provide defined examples of this cellular diversity.

An epithelial marker helps identify a cell compartment; a positive lineage stain alone does not establish malignancy or invasion. Tissue architecture matters. For an epithelial carcinoma, assessing in-situ versus invasive disease includes microscopic review of the basement membrane and surrounding tissue. The SEER summary-stage manual retains site-specific exceptions; this boundary is not a universal staging rule for every cancer.

In a fictional comparison, gene R is high in cancer cells, low in fibroblasts and similarly high in normal luminal epithelial cells. The first contrast supports higher expression than fibroblasts, even if it passes a statistical threshold; it does not establish cancer selectivity. The normal epithelial comparison addresses that claim more closely, while leaving other organs, cell states and target accessibility untested. If that reference group is tiny, contaminated or prepared differently, preserve the unresolved comparison rather than declaring selectivity or exact equality. Normal epithelial cells can also contribute familiar lineage markers to a tumour specimen. An image-based tumour mask is an assignment that needs validation for its actual method and specimens, rather than automatic proof that every included cell is malignant.

records.name: Core needle biopsy and fine-needle aspiration (FNA)
records.tldr: Core biopsy collects small cylinders of tissue; fine-needle aspiration collects cells or fluid. Both sample a site, and adequacy depends on the diagnostic question and intended tests.
records.summary: A core needle collects cylinders that preserve local tissue architecture from selected positions. Fine-needle aspiration collects cells, fluid and sometimes clusters or tissue fragments for cytology; a cell block can support additional tests without reconstructing the original full spatial map. Either method can yield diagnostically useful material, but sample adequacy, preservation and represented cells must fit the question. A readable sample may still miss the target, and enough material for diagnosis does not guarantee enough suitable material for every molecular assay.

Aspiration may recover single cells, clusters, fluid and fragments; a cell block can support additional tests but cannot reconstruct their original spatial map. Adequacy for diagnosis does not guarantee adequacy for every ancillary assay.

For each sample, retain site, collection time, prior treatment, image target, preservation, represented cells, intended assay and remaining material. Core length or count alone does not establish tumour content, whole-lesion representation or surgical margins.

A hollow cutting needle removes a narrow tissue cylinder from an image-defined target. The preserved arrangement can show an interface where it is actually present, like a plug through cake layers. Tissue is irregular and handling can damage it. A long core of scar or normal tissue does not establish tumour content.

NRG-BR005 found only half of surgically confirmed residual cancers using its post-neoadjuvant multiple-core procedure in 101 evaluable women. This is a selected breast protocol result, not a universal sensitivity for core biopsy in every organ or setting.

Core sampling starts by locating a target, collecting cylinders from the documented site, preserving them and examining sections. Diagnosis, represented architecture and any subsequent biomarker results describe those samples; core count is an inventory measure. Sectioning and extraction use finite material, and each additional assay needs a suitable validated input. A missed target, too few relevant cells, damaged cores, necrosis or incompatible preservation may defeat the intended question. Adequacy has no universal core-count threshold, and a core cannot establish whole-lesion composition, complete surgical margins or future treatment benefit.

Aspiration uses a thin needle to recover cells or fluid, including clusters and small fragments. Cytology examines shapes, nuclei and groupings. Material may be spread on slides or processed into a cell block for sections and ancillary tests when suitable. A cell block does not reconstruct the lesion-wide spatial map.

An inadequate aspirate and a negative adequate aspirate are different results. Rapid assessment can help collection but does not guarantee all later assays. A sampled node does not map every node. A fictional aspirate containing malignant breast cells supports a malignancy interpretation in context, but does not establish the full boundary or extent of invasion. Less architecture does not erase useful diagnostic information.

The cited Chen study retrospectively assessed breast aspirations from one academic hospital. Its reported performance and limited cell-block receptor comparisons do not supply universal sensitivity for every organ, team or ancillary assay.

Fine-needle aspiration collects cells or fluid from a documented site for slides or a cell block and cytologic interpretation. The report gives a diagnostic category, adequacy and any assay-specific measurements. Preparation and ancillary tests consume the finite recovered material. Cellularity and suitability depend on the organ, laboratory and intended test; too few relevant cells, blood dilution, poor preservation or a missed target can limit the result. Clinical cytology and each ancillary assay need appropriate preparation and validation. Neither the aspirate nor a research performance estimate maps unsampled tissue boundaries, the entire lesion or every lymph node.

records.name: Surgical resection specimen
records.tldr: Removed tissue becomes interpretable through documented orientation and sampling that link microscopic and molecular findings to their locations.
records.summary: A resection specimen is removed tissue submitted for examination. The laboratory documents gross features, marks relevant surfaces and maps selected regions into labelled blocks. Microscopy and additional assays describe the represented material, rather than every cell remaining in the body.

notes: Keep the specimen site, procedure, prior treatment, orientation key, surface inks, cassette map and tested block with the result. Ink colours have a local documented meaning. Gross specimen dimensions are not automatically invasive tumour dimensions. Fragmentation or ink entering cracks can complicate surface interpretation.

Fictional example: block A is central lesion and block B is a superior surface. A sequencing result from block A cannot be assigned to block B merely because both came from one operation. An additional test needs its own block identity and preservation history.

Resection supports assessment of represented tumour extent, surfaces, sampled nodes and treatment effect. A large specimen is not automatically examined cell by cell in its entirety. Collection time and preceding treatment define the biological time point, so a post-treatment resection cannot substitute for a pretreatment biopsy.

Diagnostic orientation and mapped sampling must remain intact when additional material is allocated. A research aliquot needs its site, block, preservation, treatment context and permissions. Slide counts alone do not establish the completeness of representation; a clear examined margin does not settle every clinical question.

Resection examination follows receipt and orientation, gross description, block mapping, microscopic examination and integration of findings. Record the named specimen and separately submitted parts; sectioning and extraction consume finite material. Depending on the cancer, specimen and treatment setting, outputs include diagnoses, dimensions and distances in millimetres, described margins and sampled-node counts. Lost orientation, fragmentation, ink penetration, incomplete mapping and unsuitable preservation can limit interpretation. Applicable diagnostic protocols and clinical correlation govern the report, while a research aliquot needs its own provenance. No specimen report examines every tissue left in the body or every unsampled node, or supplies an individual recurrence probability.

records.name: Analytical versus clinical validation
records.tldr: Analytical validity concerns whether a test measures reliably. Clinical validity concerns what its result means for a condition or outcome. Clinical utility concerns using that information for a decision.
records.summary: Analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility address different questions for a specified assay, specimen, population and intended use. MedlinePlus Genetics distinguishes detection of a genetic variant, its relationship to disease presence or risk, and whether the information helps diagnosis, treatment, management or prevention. Reliable measurement does not by itself establish clinical meaning, and an outcome association does not establish benefit from changing care. For a prediction model, reproducibility of fixed-input output, discrimination, calibrated probabilities and the consequences of model-guided decisions also require distinct evidence. These are related questions rather than a universal sequence that guarantees a useful test.

notes: Start a claim worksheet with the population and treatment setting, specimen and method version, measured or predicted outcome, time horizon and proposed decision. A molecule measurement, drug ranking in a dish and outcome prediction from earlier patients are different claims. For risk, retain whether the estimate assumes usual care or no treatment; for a drug experiment, retain the drug, dose and combination. Leave unavailable details unknown. Then separate the tested material and quality, biological interpretation and alternatives, prediction, proposed action and evidence of benefit. Mark each measured, inferred, proposed or unknown. A sound measurement does not automatically support the later steps.

Consider a fictional report that calls a protein-rich stored tumour a Drug A responder. Its study related protein abundance to shrinkage among people all receiving Drug A for advanced Cancer X. The measurement and response association can be useful, but there is no untreated or alternative-treatment comparison establishing greater benefit from A. Applying it after surgery also changes the setting. Ask what comparison shows improved outcomes from choosing A with this result in the proposed setting. Confirmation of protein abundance answers whether that signal is real, while postoperative benefit remains a separate question. A favourable prognostic result does not itself justify omitting standard treatment.

An evidence card records population, stage, treatment context and selection; specimen, handling, assay version and quality criteria; the reference condition or care comparator and its limitations; outcome and measurement time; the analysis plan, all tuning and independent evaluation; failed samples, dropout and missing outcomes; and sample size, intervals and remaining uncertainty. A response endpoint is not recurrence or survival. A preclinical card names the actual model and tested claim; an observational clinical association retains possible confounding. Neither alone establishes that the proposed clinical action helps. A headline metric also needs the consequences of false positive and false negative calls attached to the action. Distinguish prespecified analyses from exploratory searches, keep their tuning history, and seek confirmation that does not reuse the search. State whether a treatment-study denominator includes everyone assigned, only those treated or only those evaluable.

For analytical performance, request the detection limit with its target level, input amount, specimen and detection probability; precision within runs and across days, operators, instruments and reagent lots; agreement with an appropriate independent reference; attempted-sample failure rate and reasons; and specimen handling, preservation and interference testing. The 2017 AMP/CAP recommendations concern next-generation sequencing panels for somatic variants. They ask for performance by variant class and relevant reference materials, depth and sample numbers. They describe a lower detection limit at which 95 per cent of samples are reliably detected, but also explain why observing 19 or 20 successes in 20 trials does not by itself establish that reliability with confidence. This is an assay-specific example, not a universal validation protocol. Fresh and delayed specimens can differ, and measurement variation must be understood before interpreting a trend. Self-agreement alone does not establish accuracy.

Put the decision before ordering. Write what positive, negative, uncertain and failed results would change, including proposed treatment omission, confirmation or another sample. Compare existing pathology and other tests, and record the decision deadline, finite tissue, time, travel, uncertainty and financial burden. Name who interprets the result, who owns the clinical recommendation and when further testing is unlikely to help that decision. A result arriving after the decision closes may not serve its intended use. The worksheet exposes assumptions rather than calculating a treatment choice; urgency does not establish validity.

In the fictional postoperative protein-test case, possible next steps are checking the actual companion-diagnostic requirement and whether this assay meets it, inspecting the Drug A evidence, considering a trial of the relevant strategy, or declining a tissue-consuming test that would not change the decision. The exact laboratory, service, version and intended use matter. A research-use label, laboratory certification, development designation or report drug list cannot replace the claim-specific evidence. A companion test is tied to specified treatment use. Clinician-led off-label use, access, payment and suitability are additional questions, not promises made by a molecular report. Fast-track and breakthrough-therapy designations are not marketing approval; accelerated approval is a distinct approval pathway, not just a development designation.

Research can have a defined value without selecting treatment: checking a mechanism, explaining discordant assays or generating a future hypothesis. Name the reviewer and what would count as a useful answer rather than extending an endless chain of tests. Attribute unpublished company data and state which methods and results were available to inspect; unavailable evidence does not prove the claim false. In a fictional high/low recurrence-risk test for which neither answer changes recommended care and no relevant study is open, the immediate value for that treatment decision is limited. A separate research or personal-information goal should be weighed against burden, uncertainty and alternatives. A changed treatment decision is not itself demonstrated benefit and can add unnecessary treatment.

records.name: Multi-omic integration
records.tldr: Multi-omic integration analyses measurements from different molecular layers, such as DNA, RNA and protein, side by side while keeping track of what each one measured and which specimen it came from.
records.summary: A DNA change, an RNA count and a protein or phosphorylation measurement answer different questions, so integration starts with an evidence record for each measurement: the patient or experimental unit, specimen, collection time, tissue region, method, units and quality limits. Measurements from one specimen are paired; measurements from separate cohorts are not, and even adjacent tissue sections do not hold identical cells. Three reports that copy one DNA call add no new layer, and a value predicted by a model, such as RNA imputed from an image, must stay labelled as imputed beside measured values. Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (Argelaguet and colleagues, 2018) is one research method: it infers hidden factors that capture biological and technical sources of variability, separates axes shared across data types from axes specific to one, and can impute missing data; the authors applied it to 200 samples of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia profiled for somatic mutations, RNA expression, DNA methylation and ex vivo drug response. A factor is a statistical pattern, not a mechanism or a validated test. Technical variation needs its own handling: Risso and colleagues (2014) showed that usual RNA sequencing normalisation mostly accounts for sequencing depth and fails to correct library preparation and other unwanted technical effects, and where treatment time and processing method always change together, those data alone cannot separate their effects. In a proteogenomic study of 105 genomically annotated breast cancers, 77 of which gave high-quality data, pathway analysis of the phosphoproteome identified a G-protein-coupled receptor cluster that was not readily identified at the mRNA level (Mertins and colleagues, 2016), an example of layers adding different information. Correlation between layers is not a tested dependency, and a controlled intervention addresses a different question. Layers need not agree numerically, and disagreement is not automatically an error: bulk RNA from a mixed sample can be high for a gene whose protein, on a tissue image, sits mainly in normal vessel cells, so averaging the two into one confidence score would hide whether malignant cells carry an accessible target. Combining layers can reveal agreement, competing explanations, missing evidence or a sample mismatch, and it does not by itself show that a matching treatment will help: the ESMO Scale for Clinical Actionability of molecular Targets (2018) grades alterations in six levels of clinical evidence by their implications for patient management, from targets ready for routine decisions to investigational targets that need more data (Mateo and colleagues, 2018; a second version appeared in 2026). For a prediction model, a patient who appears in several layers must stay on one side of a patient-level split, and many cells from one biopsy are not many patients.

notes: Integration card for combining molecular layers (a reading guide, not a score). Measures: relationships among named layers, not one universal multi-omic score. How: match evidence records, check quality and comparability, harmonise features, compare or model, then evaluate the stated question. Input and tissue cost: existing assay data and metadata; computation uses no extra tissue, but each original assay has its own specimen cost. Output and units: a comparison, factors, clusters or predictions, with the model version and underlying units. Thresholds: specific to the method and validated task, and none applies to every integration. Failure modes: sample swaps, cell-mixture changes, batch confounding, missing data and information leaking into evaluation. Cannot establish alone: causation, malignant-cell target location or better treatment outcomes. Validation tier: research integration gives neither its inputs nor its resulting model a clinical status.

Figure reading (fictional): the same DNA call, a T in the sequence A C T G A, is copied into Report A, Report B and Report C, which is one observation reported three times. A separate RNA assay showing a splice junction is a new measurement that answers a new question, and it does not by itself confirm the DNA call.

Figure reading (fictional Target Q): specimen S at time T1 supplies bulk RNA, where Q is abundant, and a tissue image, where Q protein is seen in normal vessel cells. Whether malignant cells carry accessible Q is unresolved, a model-imputed Q is labelled as an estimate rather than a measurement, and a different specimen or time point is not paired evidence.

Genome, transcriptome and proteome name DNA, RNA and protein collections. An omics profile measures many features within a layer, subject to its coverage and capture limits; it does not necessarily inspect every molecule. Molecular layer and spatial or cellular resolution answer different questions. Multi-omic integration relates the measured layers, with their specimen and analysis context retained, rather than turning a larger number of assays into a universal measure of certainty.

Consider an invented repair-gene R example, with measurements attributed to the same pretreatment tissue region except for a derived model. A supported splice-site DNA variant identifies a candidate sequence change. Loss of the other allelic contribution, with the variant assigned to the retained contribution, supports a possible two-hit explanation subject to copy and phase uncertainty. A reproducible abnormal RNA junction in malignant-cell-enriched material adds evidence for a changed transcript product, while reduced staining with suitable controls adds a protein-signal difference in the assigned cells. Neither establishes that every intact protein is gone. A high genomic scar adds evidence about genomic history, not a direct test of present repair. Impaired repair in a suitable model with informative cycling and damage controls addresses function under those conditions. A replicated drug response at specified exposures adds a model-sensitivity hypothesis; it still leaves achievable safe exposure and patient benefit to their appropriate evidence. These are distinct observations, not a requirement to perform every assay before using any established clinical biomarker.

A practical report reading starts with six questions: what specimen, region, date and treatment context were sampled; what object and units were measured with which assay version; whether the result is signed clinical, preliminary, research or model-predicted evidence; which controls or reference support the comparison; what remains unmeasured; and which actual decision could change. A missing field is a question to resolve, not a fact to assume. For fictional pretreatment bulk RNA, high R relative to a stated reference supports captured expression in that mixture. Calling it a surface target remains an interpretation until the contributing cells and accessible protein are established; selectivity, dependence and treatment benefit need their own evidence. Molecular layer and resolution are separate axes. Mapping 500 RNA targets in one section adds location relative to a pooled RNA result, while the measured layer remains RNA. It does not add a membrane-protein or functional measurement. In that invented example, one pretreatment breast-biopsy region contains malignant cells and normal neighbours; no other disease site was sampled. R is reported in the assay's normalised units against a compatible reference, so high belongs to that comparison. Another broad RNA profile need not resolve the missing cell or membrane-protein location. The result can focus research follow-up; treatment selection still needs the validated biomarker-treatment link, clinical setting and eligibility.

An entirely fictional core-biopsy report lists invasive carcinoma of no special type, grade 3; ER and PR below 1 percent; HER2 IHC one-plus; Ki-67 positivity of 60 percent; stromal TILs of 30 percent; PD-L1 22C3 combined positive score 15; and a supported TP53 missense finding at VAF 38 percent on a tumour-only panel. These observations retain separate rules and denominators. The diagnosis describes the sampled region; the receptor results support a triple-negative category and low HER2 staining under the stated testing rules, without establishing a particular drug benefit. Ki-67 positivity is not a treatment-selection rule here. The stromal score is an eligible-area assessment, not proof of recognition, and CPS is its own defined stain score rather than a universal immune percentage. VAF is not inherited status, cancer-cell fraction or measured variant function. KEYNOTE-355 tested pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced TNBC; its CPS-at-least-ten group had median PFS 9.7 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.65. KEYNOTE-522 enrolled high-risk early TNBC regardless of PD-L1 status. A score cannot transfer benefit between those settings. None of these invented values is a patient observation or a prescription.
